title: Part 2 Practice: Water Resources of Ethiopia

questions.text: The LARGEST lake in Ethiopia is:
questions.explanation: LAKE TANA is Ethiopia's LARGEST lake (~3,600 km²), located in the North Central Massifs at ~1,800m elevation. It's the source of the Abay (Blue Nile) River and contains 37 islands with historic monasteries.

questions.text: Which Rift Valley lake is the DEEPEST in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: LAKE SHALLA is the DEEPEST Rift Valley lake at 266 meters. It's a soda lake (high mineral content) and is part of the Abijatta-Shalla Lakes National Park.

questions.text: Lake Langano is popular because it is:
questions.explanation: LAKE LANGANO is popular for TOURISM because it's SAFE FOR SWIMMING — it's bilharzia-free (unlike most other Ethiopian lakes). Many other Rift Valley lakes have bilharzia (schistosomiasis) parasites.

questions.text: Ethiopia's total annual surface runoff is approximately:
questions.explanation: Ethiopia's total annual surface runoff is about 122 BILLION cubic meters. This vast water resource makes Ethiopia the 'Water Tower of Africa.' However, much of it flows to neighboring countries.

questions.text: How many MAJOR river basins does Ethiopia have?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia has TWELVE major river basins: Abay, Tekeze, Baro-Akobo, Wabishebelle, Ghenalle, Awash, Omo-Ghibe, and others. The Abay basin is the largest in terms of runoff (54.5 BCM).

questions.text: GROUNDWATER in Ethiopia is stored in:
questions.explanation: GROUNDWATER is stored in AQUIFERS — porous and permeable rock formations (sandstone, fractured basalt, alluvial deposits) that can hold and transmit water. It's accessed through wells and springs.

questions.text: Ethiopia's HYDROELECTRIC potential is estimated at:
questions.explanation: Ethiopia's hydroelectric potential is estimated at 45,000 MW — the SECOND HIGHEST in Africa (after DR Congo). Currently, less than 10% is developed. The GERD alone will add 6,450 MW.

questions.text: The GERD (Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam) is on which river?
questions.explanation: The GERD is built on the ABAY (BLUE NILE) RIVER in western Ethiopia (Benishangul-Gumuz region). It will be Africa's LARGEST hydroelectric project with a capacity of 6,450 MW.

questions.text: Which lake is the LARGEST Rift Valley lake in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: LAKE ABAYA is the LARGEST Rift Valley lake in Ethiopia (1,162 km²). It's located in the southern Rift Valley and is an important fishing ground. Lake Chamo lies just south of Abaya.

questions.text: What percentage of Ethiopia's irrigation potential is currently developed?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia's irrigation potential is 3.7 million hectares, but LESS THAN 10% is currently developed. This represents a HUGE opportunity for agricultural development. Major schemes include Awash Valley and Omo Valley.
